bug_info.bug_desc: In the pre-merge FSM, the final escalation/error priority block misrouted FSM state. The global escalation branch (esc_scrap_state0_i || esc_scrap_state1_i) did not assign fsm_state_d, so asserting global escalation did not move the FSM to EscalateSt. The local state-invalid/token-if error else-if branch assigned fsm_state_d = InvalidSt but then overwrote it with fsm_state_d = EscalateSt, so local errors erroneously entered EscalateSt instead of InvalidSt. In addition, if the FSM was already in EscalateSt, the local-error branch could still fire, which was not protected by escalation priority. This broke the required behavior that global escalation takes priority and that invalid state errors lead to InvalidSt.
bug_info.fix_hint: Restructure the priority logic so global escalation is the top-priority branch and explicitly sets fsm_state_d = EscalateSt. Keep the InvalidSt assignment for local state-invalid and token_if_fsm_err conditions only when fsm_state_q is not already EscalateSt, and remove the stray fsm_state_d = EscalateSt from that invalid-error branch.
